clue.text: Belief in proof of guilt

definitions.meaning: a firmly held opinion or certainty
a court's formal finding that someone is guilty

explanation.surface: A juror's faith rests on evidence that the accused did it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a strongly held opinion and a guilty verdict delivered by a court.

clue.text: Ring-road, junction and bypass

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
M1 is the London-Leeds motorway, written MI
a T-junction gives T

explanation.surface: A ring road and a junction form a bypass.
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway; crosswords write it as MI.
explanation.definitionFit: To bypass something is to skip or leave it out.

clue.text: Check provided in actual case

indicators.note: in tells us the word for provided goes inside
case shows the word for actual acts as the outer shell

parts.note: very means actual, as in 'the very thing'
if means provided

explanation.surface: Inspect what happens in the real instance.
explanation.definitionFit: To confirm the truth of something is to check it.

clue.text: Many get mad with desire

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, many
raving means mad

explanation.surface: A crowd goes mad with longing.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong longing or yearning for something.

clue.text: Girl is to receive Religious Instruction

indicators.note: to receive means the word is takes in the other letters

parts.note: RI is the abbreviation for Religious Instruction, a school subject

explanation.surface: A girl about to attend a scripture lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name, also a flower.

clue.text: The shift that is seen after dark

indicators.note: the letters for that is appear after the word for dark

parts.note: night is the dark time
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: A night shift visible after dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' is a loose dress or chemise, not a work period.
explanation.definitionFit: A shift is a loose slip or chemise; this one is worn to bed.

clue.text: Model accommodation written about by Ibsen

definitions.meaning: a miniature home, a toy model

explanation.surface: Showhome flats described by a Norwegian dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: A child's miniature toy home, and the title of Ibsen's play about Nora.

clue.text: He is used to holding the lead

definitions.text: He is used to holding the lead

parts.words: He is used to holding the lead
parts.note: sounds like a front-runner, but describes someone holding a leash for a police or guard animal

explanation.surface: A race leader accustomed to being in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A police officer or trainer who works with a trained canine on a leash.

clue.text: Staff Officer has small house in London area

parts.note: SO is the military abbreviation for Staff Officer
HO is a shortened, 'small', form of house, as in abbreviations

explanation.surface: A military officer owns a modest home somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small house' means house in abbreviated form, HO.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of London's West End famous for nightlife and restaurants.

clue.text: Seeing what someone has to say?

definitions.text: Seeing what someone has to say?

parts.words: Seeing what someone has to say?
parts.note: normally 'seeing what someone says' means finding out; here it is literal, watching the lips to take in speech

explanation.surface: Waiting to find out what somebody will tell you.
explanation.definitionFit: Deaf people may follow speech by watching mouth movements, so they literally see words.

clue.text: Something good to drink?

parts.note: sounds like a beverage recommendation, but it is the thing we toast when we raise a glass to someone's wellbeing

explanation.surface: Asking for a recommended beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: We 'drink to someone's' wellbeing in a toast, and wellbeing is undeniably a good thing.

clue.text: Buy ring perhaps, making a grave commitment

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of the two words could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Purchasing an engagement ring is a serious pledge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns BUYRING into the answer; the surface's engagement is really an interment.
explanation.definitionFit: Committing a body to the grave is the act of interring it, a pun on serious commitment.

clue.text: Workman who naturally works his way up

definitions.text: Workman who naturally works his way up

parts.words: Workman who naturally works his way up
parts.note: sounds like an ambitious employee, but describes a builder who lays courses from the bottom upwards

explanation.surface: An ambitious worker climbing the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder sets bricks course by course, so the wall literally rises.

clue.text: A proposition showing determination

definitions.meaning: a motion put to a meeting for a vote

explanation.surface: A motion showing firm intent.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal motion voted on by a meeting, and also firmness of purpose.

clue.text: Clumsy Russian author, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the author's name spoken aloud gives the answer

parts.note: Maxim Gorky was a Russian writer

explanation.surface: A Russian writer said to be awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent the writer's surname sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Awkward and ungainly in movement.

clue.text: Cast not out to co-operate

parts.note: to cast is to throw, or pitch
a batsman not out in cricket is still in

explanation.surface: A fishing or cricket instruction about joining in.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a batsman who is not out is still 'in', batting.
explanation.definitionFit: To join in and do one's share of the work is to help together with others.

clue.text: Fruit, soft and fleshy

parts.note: a plum is a fruit
p is piano, the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A soft, fleshy fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rounded and well-padded, chubby.

clue.text: Clark's end of the house

definitions.meaning: Clark is the first name of the Hollywood actor of Gone with the Wind, so his surname is wanted
the triangular wall at the end of a pitched roof

explanation.surface: Some man called Clark owns a building's end.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gone with the Wind star's surname is also the architectural term for a triangular end wall.

clue.text: This month in Westminster

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the word Westminster

explanation.surface: Something scheduled for the current month in Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the old business-letter abbreviation for instant, meaning of the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbreviation of 'instant', used in formal letters to mean of the current month.

clue.text: For knitters the alternative is plain

definitions.text: For knitters the alternative is plain

parts.words: For knitters the alternative is plain
parts.note: reads like a simple observation, but describes the stitch that knitters use as the counterpart of plain stitch

explanation.surface: A remark that knitters have an obvious choice.
explanation.definitionFit: Knitting uses two basic stitches, plain and its reverse counterpart.

clue.text: Spare runner goes in front of politician

indicators.note: the runner piece is placed before the politician piece

parts.note: a ski is a runner on which one slides over snow
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A spare competitor leads ahead of a politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' is a verb here: to be sparing, economise.
explanation.definitionFit: To economise stingily, giving less than needed, is to be sparing.

clue.text: Furniture that provides rest, day and night

definitions.text: Furniture that provides rest, day and night

parts.words: Furniture that provides rest, day and night
parts.note: a piece for sitting on by day which converts into a sleeping place at night

explanation.surface: Furniture for relaxing around the clock.
explanation.definitionFit: A settee that folds out for sleeping, used by day and night.

clue.text: It makes a pepper pot mine, anyhow

indicators.note: anyhow says the letters of pot mine are put in any order

explanation.surface: A pepper pot produced by a mine somehow.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet red pepper, often used to stuff olives.

clue.text: There's pleasure after the game but he spoils it

indicators.note: pleasure comes after the game piece

parts.note: in hunting, the game shot is the kill
joy means pleasure

explanation.surface: Enjoyment follows a match, but someone ruins the fun.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket who dampens everyone's fun.

clue.text: Botch-up making beer for a cockney

definitions.meaning: in Cockney rhyming slang this phrase rhymes with and stands for beer

explanation.surface: Getting the brewing wrong produces a Londoner's ale.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang, from East London, swaps a word for a phrase that rhymes with it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a mess, and is London rhyming slang standing for a pint of ale.

clue.text: South-eastern woman married to a Spaniard

parts.note: Nora is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman from the south-east weds a Spaniard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as 'a married woman, to a Spaniard', the Spanish title for a wife.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish courtesy title for a wife, equivalent to Mrs or madam.

clue.text: Cause of breathing difficulty found? Hats off to mother!

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of Hats are gone wrong and rearranged

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A diagnosis discovered, and a salute to Mum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' makes ASTH from HATS; 'Hats off' looks like a tribute.
explanation.definitionFit: A chronic respiratory condition that narrows the airways and causes wheezing.

clue.text: Moist, yet may be found on fire

definitions.meaning: added to 'fire' it forms the miners' term for explosive methane gas

explanation.surface: Wet, yet possibly ablaze.
explanation.definitionFit: Slightly wet; also the gas in firedamp, the explosive methane in coal mines.

clue.text: Drum music

definitions.meaning: a cylinder on which cable or film is wound

explanation.surface: Percussion and music.
explanation.definitionFit: A spool on which thread is wound, and a lively Scottish dance tune.

clue.text: They're sharp, mind, on the cuffs

parts.note: the brain is the seat of the mind
to cuff is to box, strike with the hand

explanation.surface: Sharp-witted people mind their shirt cuffs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cuffs' is a verb, blows to the head, not shirt sleeves.
explanation.definitionFit: Clever people are called this informally, as intelligent as sharp minds.

clue.text: Cupid has painful back

indicators.note: back means the word for painful is read from end to start

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: The god of love has an aching back.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek god of love, counterpart of the Roman Cupid.

clue.text: Old beer pal in awfully bad shape

indicators.note: in, with shape, says the letters are put into a new form
shape says the fodder letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An old drinking pal is in poor condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wretched and shocking is very bad indeed.
